rationale: Argument B's core factual observation — that prep is both the runner and the auditor of --govern — is correct, but its conclusion that the spec's symmetry claim is 'architecturally false' does not follow. B claims the capture seam is protected by a cross-actor mechanical read (prep detects a missing pin). But that cross-actor detection is itself performed by prep's --govern call: if the occupant skips --capture, the only thing that catches it is --govern's pin==null unpinnable-reset branch. So the capture seam's protection is conditional on exactly the same root assumption the spec names in §7 — 'prep executes its own per-round loop steps'. If prep never runs --govern, no sidecar exists AND nothing detects either seam's omission; the spec's §7 statement ('if prep runs neither the capture assertion nor --govern, no sidecar exists for either') is precise and accurate at the deepest level, not a false symmetry. B's asymmetry exists only one level shallower, and both seams bottom out in the same irreducible assumption. The spec's defence satisfies the reconstruction's valid-solution properties: the record is CLI-written and mechanically assertable on every path --govern reaches (property 1), the failure degrades to the fail-safe (property 3), the residual 'prep never runs the loop step' case is explicitly named as a shared Assumes rather than silently unhandled (property 5), the assurance is born-verifiable via the Rev 9 SKILL-wiring lint (property 6), and the boundary is defensible against the ratified liveness precedent because the only mechanism that could audit prep from outside prep is a global Stop-hook, which §2 explicitly excludes with a regress argument (property 4). The correction B's reasoning would demand — an independent external auditor — is precisely the out-of-scope item the governing requirements exclude. Argument A offers nothing. The alleged defect reduces to a wording preference about how strongly the word 'symmetric' is scoped, with no concrete checkable failure against any governing requirement.

Argument A offers no claim or evidence, so it establishes nothing. Argument B's factual premises are partially supported but its inference fails: the reconstruction confirms the spec does make spec-review-window.js read pin-owned sidecars (pinned-reviewer.json, pin-capture.json, served-<n>.json), but the governing requirements affirmatively require exactly this data flow — the operator-ratified sidecar decision (2026-09-16) mandates that --govern read served-<n>.json as the sole served-identity source, and the valid-solution properties require the single backendIdentity() helper and the unpinnable fail-safe ordering, all of which necessitate the window module consuming pin-side state. B's predicted consequence (a future pin-sidecar schema change needing a coordinated edit in window.js, unguarded by the additive-invariant test) is speculative and hand-wavy: it names no current requirement violated, no checkable failure today, and the spec already requires per-branch tests of --govern's reads (test/spec-review-window.test.mjs asserts each branch's sidecar reads and full GovernanceResult content), so drift in the sidecar shape consumed by window is behaviourally guarded. The layering-preference claim (window should be a leaf; factory→factory edges should follow the window→convergence precedent) is a design taste with no ground truth in the governing requirements — the spec's own principles (determinism over prose, fail-safe ordering, additive-only, ratified sidecar) are all satisfied by the disputed design, and ADR-0042 per B's own quoted evidence permits factory→factory requires. No material defect is established.

Argument B's factual premises check against the reconstruction: the spec's --govern CLI surface states only '--dir/--round required' with no value constraint, in explicit contrast to --capture (where '--round is REQUIRED ... a missing --round is a usage error') and to writeWindowStart/readWindowStart (which validate window_start as an integer >= 1). The govern procedure takes n with no stated integer/>=1 gate. The inference is valid: on the unpinnable-reset path the spec orders writeWindowStart(dir, n) BEFORE the governance-<n>.json write, and on the fault paths the record write precedes writeWindowStart but both writes use the unvalidated n in a filename; a degenerate or oversized --round (0, negative, or exceeding NAME_MAX) can therefore leave a round that mutated window.json (or crashed mid-sequence) with no governance-<n>.json — directly violating the spec's own Rev 9 invariant that 'EVERY round that reaches --govern leaves an audit artifact' and its DONE criterion to that effect. The predicted consequence is concrete and checkable (window narrowed, audit record absent, prep surfaces govern-record-missing with no artifact to read), not hand-wavy taste. The correction is bounded by existing governing requirements: the spec already mandates fail-loud on under-specified invocations before any read, and already applies exactly this validation to --capture's --round and to window_start; extending the same integer >= 1 usage-error gate to --govern's --round is the minimal, in-pattern fix. Argument A offers no argued defence, so the objection stands unopposed on the merits.

correction.summary: Add explicit --round value validation to the --govern CLI surface and the govern procedure: --round must be an integer >= 1; a missing, non-integer, or < 1 --round is a usage error (exit 2, arg-validation, written before any read, no governance record) — mirroring --capture's existing --round requirement and writeWindowStart's window_start >= 1 validation, so no degenerate round value can reach writeWindowStart or the governance-<n>.json filename and break the 'every path leaves an audit artifact' invariant. Add a named test case (in test/spec-review-window.test.mjs) asserting --govern with --round 0, a negative round, and a non-integer round exits 2 as a usage error with window.json byte-unchanged and no governance record written.
correction.verification: --govern validates --round as an integer >= 1 before any read: a missing, non-integer, or < 1 --round is a usage error (exit 2, no governance record, window.json byte-unchanged)

rationale: Argument A's factual premises partially hold — there is indeed no single aggregate DONE bullet or test asserting 'every non-arg-error --capture path writes pin-capture.json' mirroring the Rev 9 --govern item — but its conclusion does not follow. First, the born-verifiable precedent requires each DONE criterion be decidable by a named test and pass condition, not that the two seams carry structurally identical aggregate test items. Every capture path is individually pinned by named tests: the no-lens skip marker (exit 0, no pin, no served-<n>.json), the {failed}-before-exit-2 path, the captured path with served-<n>.json, and the round>=2 idempotent no-op (served-<n>.json written). A build omitting pin-capture.json on any of these paths fails an existing named test, so the criterion is decidable; the missing aggregate phrasing is a stylistic asymmetry, not an undecidable criterion. Second, A's concrete predicted consequence — the idempotent no-op path 'silently omitting' pin-capture.json — is contradicted by the spec itself: §4 explicitly specifies that the no-op path leaves pin + pin-capture.json untouched BY DESIGN, with the round's record carried by served-<n>.json (a DONE bullet and a behavioural test cover exactly this). A 'records on every path' test for --capture would therefore contradict the specified behaviour, since the no-op path intentionally writes no capture marker. Third, the arg-validation error paths (missing --round, mutually exclusive flags) write no record on both seams symmetrically, matching the --govern carve-out A's own quoted invariant accepts. A's remaining concern about 'a future added capture path' is speculative and not a checkable defect against the current spec. Argument B offers no argued case. No material defect established; at most a taste-level minor about test phrasing symmetry.

Argument B's factual premises do not hold against the spec text. (1) The claimed co-occurring state (capRound == n AND served_identity != backendIdentity(pin)) is not a CLI-reachable runtime state: on the capture path the pin and served-<n>.json are written in the same call from the same chain[winnerIndex] through the same scrub(backendIdentity()) — the spec's §4 capture procedure makes them identical by construction, not merely by prose assertion. The only route to co-occurrence is out-of-band tampering, the same class the spec already handles via the Rev 6 synthetic-fixture framing and the well-formedness/fault gating on both operands. (2) The predicted consequence is not concrete or harmful: in the spec's sequential rule, if both conditions somehow fired, swap-reset would overwrite late-pin-advance with ws := n — the fail-safe direction (window narrowed to the current round, never a cross-reviewer compare). A 'double-fire' therefore cannot produce the silent false-verdict harm the ticket exists to prevent; at worst the action label is the later of the two while window_start == n, which the spec itself designates as the consumer-facing signal ('equivalently window_start == n'). (3) Under the ratified precedent (born-verifiable-decidable-not-one-dedicated-scenario-per-done-item), demanding a dedicated scenario for a constructionally-unreachable co-occurrence whose failure mode is still fail-safe is a taste-level 1:1-scenario objection — minor at most, not a material defect. Argument A's position (no argued defect) stands; the spec's §4 prose already states the distinct-events invariant, the write-path construction enforces it, and the enumerated §8 branch tests cover every reachable branch.
